original_card.question: Does the reported word-census parity-pruning error invalidate a specific exclusion we still rely on, and what bounded repair is justified?
methods: Independently reconstruct the tiny counterexample and trace one affected exclusion to its exact pruning code.
Compare corrected and unpruned enumeration on a small exhaustive domain, then audit the changed pruning implication.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the old and proposed corrected engines, distinguish a disproved pruning rule from a disproved final bound, and state exactly which downstream exclusions need revalidation. #2973 is an author-checked source archive; neither its new f(7) claim nor all old conclusions are automatically accepted or rejected.

first_step.inspect: Read #2973 error description and MATH.md; manually reconstruct the prefix states of 01021323 before running any large census.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no full enumeration or mathematical validation.

original_card.first_experiment: Reconstruct the eight prefix states of 01021323 and compare bit-0 versus Hamming-weight parity budgets independently. Trace the reported false prune to one pinned predecessor (#2542, #2634 or #2691), then test a small exhaustive domain. Stop after a source-impact handoff or corrected-prune proof; a full seven-label replay needs a separate resource budget and a named research decision it can change.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An unsound exclusion can wrongly close a mechanism; correcting its dependency boundary is more useful than extending the same census.
allowed_variations: One predecessor pruning rule, one independently exhaustive small domain, or one downstream dependency audit.
scope_change_triggers: Launching a larger census before validating the prune and explaining which active decision it changes.
Treating a small-domain counterexample to the old rule as a counterexample to every reported seven-label bound.

actual_scope: Independent complete enumeration of all five admissible n=7, L=20 weight-parity split representatives, after independently reconstructing the n=4 false-prune witness and checking the pinned predecessor code.
scope_change_reason: The original card first required a bounded counterexample, exact predecessor prune and small exhaustive domain; those gates passed in --quick. The corrected census package explicitly leaves a second complete n=7 length-20 implementation as an open question. This finite replay changes the evidence status of its f(7) >= 22 exclusion in the PR943 word model. I allocated one bounded 60-minute research session and did not start an L=22 search.
bottleneck_link: Independent completion evidence tests whether the corrected finite singleton-word lower bound can be relied on; this is separate from both selected suppliers and does not change kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after the five uncapped length-20 split runs, direct length-24 witness check, small counterexample audit and source/metadata verification. Do not search length 22 or claim a multiplier improvement.
evidence: The independent raw-word oracle finds 22 universal n=4, L=8, (4,4) canonical simple words; the pinned old budget falsely removes 6. The independent C11 replay completes five uncapped n=7, L=20 split searches with zero admissible closed leaves and zero hits at 1,170,514,704 total nodes. It directly verifies the retained length-24 upper witness. Reproduce with python3 -I -B research/f7-independent-full-replay/verify.py --full.
author: OpenAI Codex
ai_assistance: Implemented and verified by OpenAI Codex. No separate human review or proof-assistant verification is claimed.

open_questions.question: Does a restored universal seven-label word of length 22 exist?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The independently corroborated lower bound and the verified length-24 word leave only 22 or 24 as f(7) in the PR943 model.
open_questions.first_step: Derive and source-check every admissible length-22 weight-parity split and its necessary collision inequalities before authorizing any bounded search.
open_questions.blocked_by: No length-22 split classification or enumeration is included in this package.
